key_cases.case_name: S.M. v. Florida Department of Children & Families
key_cases.holding: Once grounds for termination are proved by clear and convincing evidence and reunification is not in the child's manifest best interests, the least-restrictive-means requirement does not oblige the trial court to consider permanent guardianship instead of adoption.
key_cases.relevance: Permanent guardianship is a subordinate permanency option available only after reunification and adoption are unavailable.
key_cases.quote: Section 39.621, Florida Statutes (2016), specifies that permanent guardianship shall be considered only after reunification and adoption are not available options.

key_cases.case_name: In re J.B. (J.B. v. Department of Children & Family Services)
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District
key_cases.holding: An order placing children in permanent guardianship and terminating protective supervision was reversed because the procedure used did not produce an adequate evidentiary hearing on the facts required to support permanent guardianship.
key_cases.relevance: J.B. states the evidentiary prerequisites for a permanent guardianship judgment in Florida.
key_cases.quote: the procedure used did not result in an adequate evidentiary hearing to establish the factual issues necessary to support an order of permanent guardianship

key_cases.case_name: T.L. v. Department of Children & Families
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Fourth District
key_cases.holding: The order denying the mother's motion for reunification and placing the children in permanent guardianship was reversed and the guardianship vacated because the finding that she had not substantially complied with her case plan lacked competent substantial evidence.
key_cases.relevance: Permanent guardianship cannot be imposed as a substitute for a properly decided reunification motion.
key_cases.quote: We vacate the order of permanent guardianship and reverse and remand for a new hearing on the Mother's motion for reunification.

key_cases.case_name: Department of Children & Families v. C.W.
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, First District
key_cases.holding: On remand the trial court properly reweighed the section 39.810 manifest-best-interests factors, and its decision to deny termination and change the permanency goal to placement with a fit and willing relative was affirmed as supported by competent substantial evidence.
key_cases.relevance: Placement with a fit and willing relative is a permissible permanency outcome when termination is not in the child's manifest best interests.
key_cases.quote: Finding that the trial court's order is based on competent substantial evidence, we affirm.
